item.title: An In-depth Study of Stochastic Stellarator Coil Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.33374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend stochastic coil optimization for stellarators and analyze the effect of optimizing for coil manufacturing errors, assembly errors represented by centroid translations and angular offsets, and errors in the coil currents. We further analyze the impact of different perturbation methods and use them in conjunction with the Augmented Lagrangian algorithm. For three stellarators, we show that stochastic methods regularize the coil optimization landscape and improve robustness in every case, with the magnitude of the improvement varying substantially across different plasmas. Our metric for coil robustness, $Q$, is improved by $4.50\%$ to $729\%$ across different configurations. Lastly, we perform numerous hyperparameter scans, including e.g. scanning the training perturbation size and the out-of-sample (OOS) evaluation perturbation size and find coupled and de-coupled training tolerance gains ranging from $0.09$ mm to $1.35$ mm depending strongly on the particular stellarator.
item.dc:creator: Vincenzo Gallegos, Evan Laljit, Julianne Stratton, Gabe Perez-Giz, Alan Kaptanoglu

item.title: A Novel Linked-Mirror Device for Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.33529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design a novel linked-mirror device (LMD) with a magnetic well using the near-axis expansion (NAE) method. The design consists of two parallel straight mirror sections connected at both ends by three-dimensional stellarator-like magnetic fields , thereby eliminating the end-loss problem of a single magnetic mirror. By designing appropriate three-dimensional magnetic fields, we obtain an LMD configuration with a magnetic well, ensuring stability against interchange modes. The existence of finite-\b{eta} equilibria of the LMD is demonstrated by numerical solutions of the 3D equilibrium code GVEC. This design is potentially a novel solution to magnetic confinement for fusion reactors.
item.dc:creator: Haorong Qiu, Xiang Li, Guodong Yu, Zhexuan Zheng, Caoxiang Zhu, Guoyong Fu

item.title: Accelerating high-fidelity gyrokinetic fusion simulations with iGENE
item.description: arXiv:2610.33561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the latest version of iGENE, a differentiable implementation of the local (flux-tube) gyrokinetic code GENE, now fully rewritten in JAX. iGENE features a multispecies, collisional, fully electromagnetic nonlinear gyrokinetic model while preserving end-to-end differentiability. The code is verified against GENE for linear ITG, TEM and KBM physics and for nonlinear turbulent fluxes with adiabatic and kinetic electrons. Forward-mode derivatives of the linear growth rate agree with finite differences for all five parameters tested, resolving the 30--50\% discrepancy in $\hat{s}$ and $\epsilon$ reported for the earlier TensorFlow version. All collectives are native JAX operations, and the code strong-scales from 2 to 32 H100 GPUs with 86\% parallel efficiency. We then assess three routes to a shorter time to solution. Custom CUDA FFT kernels operating in bfloat16 are up to $3.97\times$ faster than fp32 cuFFT on the transforms, and on a single H100 iGENE is $2.63\times$ faster per time step than single-precision GENE. Multi-rate sub-cycling of the parallel dynamics yields a further $1.89\times$ speedup with kinetic electrons. Finally, a Hermite-Laguerre velocity-space representation is implemented, offering tunable fidelity.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Merlo, Victor Artigues, Carl-Martin Pfeiler, Frank Jenko

item.title: Triple Decomposition of Field Gradient Tensors in Space Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2610.33563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Characterizing local topology in magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence is fundamental to understanding energy dissipation, intermittency, and coherent structures in space plasmas. Classical double decomposition of velocity ($A_{ij}$) and magnetic ($Z_{ij}$) field gradient tensors into symmetric strain and anti-symmetric rotation components conflates rigid-body rotation with planar sliding shear. Here, we extend the real-Schur-based Triple Decomposition framework to MHD flows, rigorously isolating irrotational normal strain ($N, M$), residual pure shear ($H, K$), and true rigid-body rotation ($R, B$). Applying this method to high-resolution NASA-MMS multi-spacecraft observations in the solar wind and Earth's magnetosheath reveals distinct topological signatures. Solar wind dynamics are predominantly strain-dominated due to spherical radial expansion, whereas magnetosheath turbulence is overwhelmingly shear-dominated, driven by boundary interactions. Crucially, cross-term contributions ($2RH$ and $2KB$) are suppressed to $\le 7\%$ across both plasma regimes, contrasting sharply with neutral fluid turbulence ($\sim 13\%$). This suppression is driven by background magnetic-field-induced anisotropy ($k_\perp \gg k_\parallel$), which confines shearing motions perpendicular to the primary rotation axes. By cleanly separating genuine vortex cores from current sheets and shear layers, the Triple Decomposition provides an objective framework for characterizing plasma turbulence and analyzing data from future multi-spacecraft missions.
item.dc:creator: Virgilio Quattrociocchi, Giuseppe Consolini, Maria Federica Marcucci

item.title: Wave-branch classification of ideal MHD discontinuities in Q-variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.33787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $Q$-variable formalism combines velocity and magnetic field into branches aligned with a selected MHD wave. For homogeneous ideal MHD, appropriate choices of the branch parameter $\alpha$ correspond to the fast, Alfv\'en, and slow characteristic families, with the background variables $\boldsymbol{Q}_0^{\pm}$ representing the propagation direction and speed of the corresponding characteristics. In structured plasmas, $\alpha$ may instead be selected from the dispersion relation of a global mode such as a kink wave. Recent work reformulated the ideal-MHD Rankine-Hugoniot conditions in $Q$-variables and established their exact equivalence with the classical conservative jump conditions. Here, we apply this formulation to the standard ideal-MHD discontinuity catalogue. We determine how the two discontinuity-frame branches $\boldsymbol{Q}^{\prime+}$ and $\boldsymbol{Q}^{\prime-}$, their sums, and their $\alpha$-normalised differences are constrained across contact, tangential, and rotational discontinuities and across the principal shock families. Material interfaces are distinguished by their normal branch content, rotational discontinuities by an Alfv\'enic tangential relation, and fast, slow, and intermediate shocks by the magnitude or orientation of the $\alpha$-normalised tangential branch difference. Perpendicular, parallel, switch-on, and switch-off shocks appear as geometrical or limiting cases. The resulting classification expresses the classical discontinuity conditions in a wave-aligned form and, through the characteristic interpretation of $\boldsymbol{Q}_0^{\pm}$, shows how ideal-MHD discontinuities constrain changes in characteristic propagation direction and speed across the interface. It therefore establishes the background interface structure required for subsequent studies of reflection, transmission, coupling, and mode conversion.
item.dc:creator: Anna Krupka, Tom Van Doorsselaere

item.title: Non-Ideal Relativistic Plasma Mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2610.33796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Relativistic plasma mirrors formed in the wake of intense laser pulses propagating in underdense plasmas can provide an efficient mechanism for generating attosecond pulses, and for enhanced focusing towards ultra-high intensity fields. We derive the reflection coefficient of a laser pulse interacting with relativistic mirrors, assuming different density profiles for the mirror. Analytical expressions are obtained for flat-top and parabolic density mirrors, and in the Dirac-delta limit, demonstrating the strong dependence of the reflectivity on the plasma mirror density profile. Fully kinetic multi-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations and our analytical model confirm that the density spike at the rear of the plasma bubble exhibits an approximately parabolic profile. Our results show that a laser wakefield setup can be optimized to maximize the reflection coefficient under specific laser driver conditions, determined by the balance between the moving plasma mirror proper density, thickness, and relativistic momentum carried by the mirror.
item.dc:creator: Zahra M. Chamazkoti, Lu\'is O. Silva

item.title: Generalization of the Rosenbluth-Putvinski avalanche growth rate to the drift kinetic regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.33917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new collisionless detrapping mechanism is shown to modify the rate of runaway electron (RE) generation by as much as a factor of two for strong inductive electric fields. This detrapping mechanism results from the magnetic well inherent to tokamak geometry being tilted by the strong inductive electric fields present during tokamak disruptions. The impact of this collisionless detrapping mechanism is found to be described by a single dimensionless parameter, whose identification enables the transition between distinct regimes of RE generation to be characterized. Using this composite parameter, it is shown that modifications to the avalanche growth rate by tokamak geometry across a broad range of plasma parameters collapse onto a one-dimensional curve that can be accurately fit with a two parameter function. The resulting analytical formula extends the classic Rosenbluth-Putvinski avalanche growth rate expression beyond the bounce-averaged limit into RE regimes where collisionless detrapping strongly modifies RE generation rates.
item.dc:creator: Christopher J. McDevitt, Jonathan S. Arnaud

item.title: Identification of rippling interface between laser-ablated plasma and ambient uniform plasma at rest
item.description: arXiv:2610.34057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present laboratory experiments on the early stage of the formation process of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks using laser-produced plasmas in an ambient uniform nitrogen (N) gas with 1~Torr under the external magnetic field with controlled polarity. An expanding aluminum (Al) piston plasma arising from laser irradiation interacts with a magnetized ambient N plasma, producing a bright, asymmetric self-emission whose global morphology reverses with the magnetic-field polarity. Two-dimensional ideal-magnetohydrodynamics simulations reproduce the main features of the observed structures and indicate that the ripple formation is unlikely to be driven by the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, but is instead associated with vortex formation at the rounded leading edge of the piston plasma. We show that the bright, rippling emission delineates the Al-N interface, whose intrinsic width is consistent with an electron kinetic scale, and that its upstream side is predominantly composed of N plasma. This identification allows the formation of a supercritical collisionless shock in the magnetized N plasma to be discussed with minimal Al contamination.

item.title: Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock
item.description: arXiv:2610.34058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks require ion reflection for dissipation, yet its role during formation remains unclear. Using high-power lasers, self-emission imaging, and collective Thomson scattering, we investigate a forming quasi-perpendicular shock. An upstream emission tail is consistent with a foot-like structure, while ion heating and temperature anisotropy extend upstream of a ramp-like region. These observations provide evidence of reflected-ion-related heating during early shock formation, although the incident and reflected ion populations are not separately resolved. Future measurements of ion distributions and plasma waves could clarify how this heating mediates shock dissipation and particle energization.

item.title: Laser wakefield acceleration and x-ray emission in plasma produced by the electrical explosion of an aluminum wire
item.description: arXiv:2610.34859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Underdense plasmas used in relativistic laser-plasma interactions are conventionally produced from gaseous targets, whereas low-density metallic plasmas remain comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate the interaction of a femtosecond petawatt laser with expanded aluminum plasma using particle-in-cell simulations based on an experimentally motivated exploding-wire density profile. Three-dimensional simulations show that the laser propagates through the low-density metallic plasma, drives a pronounced wake-like structure, accelerates electrons to near-GeV energies, and produces directional broadband x-ray emission. Charge-state-resolved diagnostics further show that electrons associated with higher aluminum ionization stages are disproportionately represented in the energetic population. Complementary two-dimensional simulations indicate that the net electron energy gain is dominated by longitudinal electric-field work and show that relativistic electron generation persists under variations of the assumed initial ionization and density conditions, although the yield remains quantitatively sensitive to the plasma state. These results demonstrate the feasibility of electrically exploded aluminum plasma as a target platform for laser wakefield acceleration and associated x-ray generation.
item.dc:creator: Heng Wang, Liang Sheng, Jun Liu, Yang Li, Yanfei Li, Xinjian Tan, Dongwei He

item.title: Toward Integrated Microwave Diagnostics for Future Fusion Devices: Design of a Compact Waveguide Diplexer
item.description: arXiv:2610.34881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Microwave diagnostics are essential for plasma control and physics studies in magnetic confinement fusion, providing measurements of electron density, electron temperature, and energetic-particle behavior. However, diagnostic access in future burning-plasma reactors will be severely constrained by breeding blankets, neutron shielding, and compact reactor geometries, requiring reduced blanket opening areas while maintaining diagnostic capability. This work presents a compact waveguide diplexer for front-end integration of multiple microwave diagnostics. The proposed diplexer combines a waveguide T-junction with two iris-coupled sixth-order Chebyshev bandpass filters, enabling microwave reflectometry and electron cyclotron emission (ECE) diagnostics to share a common transmission line while operating in separate frequency bands. As an initial study, the diplexer is designed for the 65-70 GHz reflectometry and 85-90 GHz ECE systems on the J-TEXT tokamak. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate insertion losses below 1 dB and channel isolation exceeding 40 dB across both operating bands. The proposed methodology provides a compact and scalable approach to microwave diagnostic integration and establishes a practical basis for multi-diagnostic front-end systems in future fusion devices.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoliang Li, Valerian Hall-Chen, Umesh Kumar, Eddie Chua, Tengfei Tang, Andy Yeoh, Khadija Rahman, Xinhang Xu, Yilun Zhu

item.title: Non-Maxwellianity in Temperature Relaxation between Plasma Species
item.description: arXiv:2610.35009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temperature relaxation between plasma species is usually described by Landau--Spitzer (LS) theory, which assumes Maxwellian distributions throughout. We show analytically that, for two Maxwellian species in homogeneous isotropic plasmas, the interspecies collisions driving relaxation generate a universal three-lobe initial distortion and that these distortions initially reduce energy exchange over a broad parameter range. Full Fokker--Planck simulations reveal substantial relaxation delays when interspecies deformation competes with self-thermalization. For post-shock deuterium--tritium plasmas relevant to inertial confinement fusion, with $T_{\mathrm{T}}/T_{\mathrm{D}}=1.5$, the relaxation time exceeds the LS prediction by 47%. The accompanying distortions lower the apparent DD/DT temperature ratio and produce positive DD and negative DT Gamow-shift residuals relative to Maxwellian predictions. These results also motivate examining non-Maxwellianity in fuel heating by fusion $\alpha$ particles.
item.dc:creator: Yao Guo, Dong Wu, Jie Zhang

item.title: Bright Compton source based on the interaction of an ultraintense laser pulse with a relativistically transparent foil and a plasma mirror
item.description: arXiv:2610.35039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and numerically study an x-ray source in which a single laser pulse first accelerates electrons while passing through a relativistically transparent thin overdense foil and then, after reflection from a plasma mirror, collides head-on with them. Two-dimensional kinetic simulations show that for a laser pulse with an intensity of the order of $10^{21}$~W/cm$^2$ and optimal foil parameters, electrons are accelerated to energies of the order of 100~MeV, and the source can deliver up to $10^{7}$ photons per 0.1\% bandwidth per joule of laser energy in the 10--250~keV range, two orders of magnitude more than a similar gas-jet scheme. This also exceeds the spectral yield per joule of the best gas-target betatron sources by about an order of magnitude and is comparable to the best experimental results obtained with near-critical-density targets.
item.dc:creator: Daria A. Chekmareva, Artem V. Korzhimanov

item.title: Explosive instability, quiet plasma: phase-space cascades, coherent vortices, and transport suppression in a dipole pair plasma
item.description: arXiv:2610.35048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turbulence in a magnetised dipole pair plasma can transfer electrostatic energy into coherent flows while carrying entropy to small scales. This occurs via a dual cascade in a four-dimensional phase space, whereby advection by the fluctuating electric field nonlinearly phase-mixes the transit-averaged particle motion. Below a critical pressure gradient, zonal bands suppress the kinetic mode, leaving a transport floor. When the fluid mode is unstable, an explosive burst collapses into a zonal condensate on which two vortices "breathe" by reversible energy exchange, without causing net transport.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Kennedy, Gabriel G Plunk

item.title: Drift wave turbulence and transport analysis of hot ion L-mode plasma with fishbone instability on the HL-3 tokamak
item.description: arXiv:2610.35072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the cross-scale coupling by which a fishbone mode governs both toroidal rotation and drift-wave turbulence in the HL-3 hot ion mode ($T_i \approx 3T_e$, $T_i(0)\approx9.8$\,keV). Combining multi-diagnostic measurements, OMFIT modeling, and TGLF simulations, we show that under 2.5\,MW co-injected NBI a steep fast-ion pressure gradient excites an $m=1,n=1$ fishbone mode. The mode redistributes resonant fast ions outward and decouples the NBI torque, and the sawtooth crash it triggers collapses the rotation from above $100$ to $60$\,krad/s. The same fast ions drive the fishbone and stabilize ion scale ITG/TEM turbulence. Their redistribution lowers the instability threshold and erodes the internal transport barrier. The effective ITG threshold combines a dominant temperature-ratio term, a fast-ion dilution factor, and an $E\times B$ shear term. TGLF scans show the high $T_i/T_e$ ratio suppresses all transport fluxes, synergistically with the fast-ion population. A single macroscopic MHD mode governs both momentum balance and microturbulence stability.
item.dc:creator: Y. K. Shu, W. Chen, Z. J. Li, S. Xu, Y. F. Liu, B. L. Hao, Z. Wang, D. L. Yu, S. S. Yang, W. Y. Zhai, X. L. Zhu, P. W. Shi, X. L. Xu, T. Wu, Z. B. Shi, HL-3 Team

item.title: Kinetic modifications to parallel transport in a low-recycling scrape-off layer: A one dimensional gyrokinetic study
item.description: arXiv:2610.35455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A liquid lithium boundary offers a route to improved energy confinement via reduced recycling, but the resulting low-density, high-temperature edge can become sufficiently collisionless such that standard fluid models are no longer applicable. Experimental measurements of scrape-off-layer (SOL) parameters, including density decay length ($\lambda_n$) estimates presented here can be used for simple analytic estimates of kinetic effects, but need more complete kinetic treatment. We present gyrokinetic simulations, with one configuration-space dimension and two velocity-space dimensions, of low and higher-recycling LTX-$\beta$ SOL conditions using Gkeyll, an open-source continuum gyrokinetic code. The simulations follow a single open field line, self-consistently evolving kinetic ion and electron distribution functions, electrostatic potential, collisions, sources, and sheath losses constrained by experimental midplane measurements. The hotter low-recycling case develops a larger parallel potential variation, and a density response not captured by an adiabatic Boltzmann-electron closure of the field equations, demonstrating the importance of kinetic electrons and the ambipolar potential in reducing electron end losses. Collisionality scans show that, as ion neoclassical collisionality falls below unity, the ion distribution develops pronounced non-Maxwellian features. The corresponding SOL particle and energy confinement times increase at low collisionality, particularly for low recycling, because ions become mirror-trapped and electron losses are throttled by the ambipolar potential. These results indicate that low-recycling lithium boundaries in LTX-$\beta$ access a regime where mirror trapping and electrostatic confinement fundamentally alter parallel residence times relative to conventional fluid expectations, an effect expected to be more pronounced in larger devices.
item.dc:creator: A. Maan, E. Perez, M. Francisquez, M. Dorf, D. P. Boyle, R. Majeski, A. Hakim, G. W. Hammett

item.title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, Carlo Presilla

item.title: Relativistic Space-Charge-Limited Current in Electrostatic Limit for a Finite-Width Diode with Arbitrary Injection Energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.35625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a weakly relativistic and electrostatic formulation of space-charge-limited current (SCLC) with arbitrary injection energy, covering the accelerating-diode and drift-space regimes. The one-dimensional (1D) relativistic SCLC model is obtained from a stationary-current condition, which is validated against the numerical solutions. Based on this relativistic 1D SCLC model, we investigate two different approaches to account for the effects of finite emission area for a two-dimensional (2D) planar diode of a finite width of $W$, which is larger than the gap spacing $D$. The field-balance (FB) approach evaluates the opposing space-charge fields at the potential minimum, whereas the density-weighted (DW) approach uses the mean absolute distance of electrons from that minimum. The two approaches yield different corrections at finite injection energy, even in the non-relativistic limit, with FB model predicting a larger leading-order enhancement. DW model reproduces our previously published classical coefficient and the classical drift-space limit, whereas the FB model gives a different result. Note both approaches are identical for zero injection velocity. Comparisons with 2D electrostatic particle-in-cell (ES-PIC) simulations, it is found that FB and DW model show better agreement for higher injection energy (= gap voltage) at smaller and larger $W/D$ emission area respectively.
item.dc:creator: Y. L. Liu, S. W. Choo, L. K. Ang

item.title: On the Energy Minimizing Problem in Plasma Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.33040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fundamental question in plasma physics and its applications to fusion theory is to find minimum energy stares of plasma.. Hong Qin has suggested the use of what he calls "Gromov ground states" which take into account the phenomenon of symplectic rigidity, as opposed to Gardner's classical approach which only use volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. Howev4er Qin's approach leads to topological difficulties because his constructions remain in the classical (Hamiltonian) domain. We circumvent these difficulties by introducing a quantum-mechanical formulation of the problem, based on the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian state
item.dc:creator: Maurice de Gosson

item.title: Trapped sausage modes in magnetic pores: existence criteria and viscous damping
item.description: arXiv:2610.33251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The conditions governing the existence and evolution of trapped sausage waves in photospheric magnetic pores are investigated, with particular emphasis on the limitations of analytical cut-off criteria and the role of viscous dissipation. A pore is modelled as a cylindrical magnetic flux tube with smoothly varying radial profiles of magnetic field and density, subject to the constraint that its temperature is lower than that of the surrounding atmosphere. For finite plasma-$\beta$, the linearised equations governing sausage-mode perturbations are derived, and an initial-value problem is solved numerically to obtain the full spatio-temporal evolution of the waves. The applicability of the analytical cut-off relation derived for a flux tube with step-function equilibrium profiles is examined, revealing that its predictions depend on the equilibrium parameters. The simulations reveal distinct wave behaviours across different parameter regimes, including the simultaneous excitation of trapped fast and slow sausage waves for a representative photospheric parameter set. Viscous damping is further investigated through the temporal evolution of the wave energy. Energy dissipation increases with decreasing viscous Reynolds number, increasing longitudinal wavenumber, and increasing radial magnetic-field contrast. These trends are consistent with enhanced viscous damping associated with increasingly fine spatial gradients generated through phase mixing. The findings highlight the importance of radial equilibrium structure in assessing sausage-wave trapping and demonstrate the sensitivity of wave-energy dissipation to the physical parameters of photospheric magnetic pores.
item.dc:creator: Zanyar Ebrahimi

item.title: Magnetic switchback development from the evolution of torsional Alfv\'en waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.34518v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic switchbacks are mostly Alfv\'enic local deflections, or even reversals, of the ambient magnetic field of the solar wind. Despite intense research their origin remains unclear and is highly debated. Here we describe a new simulation study demonstrating how torsional Alfv\'en waves can evolve into switchbacks. We use surface rotational motions to launch torsional Alfv\'en waves into the super-radially expanding magnetic field of a coronal hole. The simulations demonstrate that in such an expanding wind, the waves initially steepen as they propagate while also inducing a cylindrical parallel plasma jet. A combination of shear from the jet and wave evolution under the constraint of approximate spherical polarisation ($|\mathbf{B}|\approx const.$) then leads to the formation of switchbacks in a ring configuration. We explore the 3D nature of the switchbacks, how and where they from, and present scalings for their peak deflection and parallel and perpendicular length scales. We also derive an expression for switchback deflection in the linear regime which we contrast against our results. The results are discussed in relation to recent observations and previous switchback formation studies.
item.dc:creator: Peter F Wyper, Etienne Pariat, Lorenzo Matteini, Jonathan Squire, Jade Touresse

item.title: Maximization of accelerated charge in multibunch-driven plasma wakefield accelerators
item.description: arXiv:2610.35049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driving the plasma wakefield with a train of multiple particle bunches has the potential to significantly increase the accelerated charge, provided that the witness bunches also form a train. In this scenario, the driver bunches can replenish the wave energy after the passage of the witness bunches, yielding comparable charges in both trains. However, implementing this method at high wakefield amplitudes is complicated by the reshaping of the driver bunches as they reach radial equilibrium with the wave. The witness bunches cannot preserve their quality during this process; nevertheless, they must load the wave to prevent it from reaching the amplitude at which the wakefield period elongates and the wave destroys the driver. The proposed solution is to form an equilibrium train of initially inefficient driver bunches, which becomes efficient upon the injection of the witness bunches. This concept is demonstrated using the example of a self-modulating driver beam. Several factors favoring a high witness charge are identified: injecting additional ``phaser'' bunches at the zero-accelerating-field points, suppressing the formation of an electron halo around the plasma, and operating at the highest possible wakefield amplitudes.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Lotov

item.title: Effects of Pulse Duration on Kerr Self-Focusing and Weld Formation in Ultrafast Laser Welding of Fused Silica
item.description: arXiv:2610.35250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kerr self-focusing can shift the laser interaction region away from the geometrical focus, making energy deposition near the joining interface difficult to control. Here, the effect of pulse duration on nonlinear focusing and weld formation is investigated from 262 fs to 10 ps. ICCD imaging shows clear changes in the axial position and shape of the plasma emission. Different pulse durations already produce distinct axial positions during the initial 2000 pulses, and these positions continue to evolve with pulse accumulation. The final weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength show corresponding changes. A ray-optics model including the Kerr effect is used to calculate the focal shift. The simulated trend agrees with the experiment and supports the role of Kerr self-focusing in the observed focal position change. These results clarify the relationship between pulse duration, nonlinear focusing, interaction position, and weld formation.
item.dc:creator: Chen Yitong, Li Nan, Han Zhijie, Li Yuxuan, Zhang Qingwei, Dong Zihui, Sun Yuming, Lin Zhe, Zhu Gangyi, Yang Shanglu

item.title: Self-consistent flow maps based on commutator-free exponential integrators
item.description: arXiv:2610.35327v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a flow-map framework for nonlinear transport equations, comprising a self-consistent exact frozen flow and its numerical realization. An exponential--pullback identity represents each frozen transport exponential in a commutator-free exponential integrator as the pullback induced by its exact backward characteristic map. Composing these maps defines the self-consistent exact frozen flow, a time-discrete construction with autonomous frozen fields formed from linear combinations of transport fields evaluated at the stage approximations. A local freezing-error identity and a one-step estimate for the Lie--Euler Vlasov--Poisson update separate field variation, field approximation, and characteristic integration errors; these estimates do not assert global PDE convergence. We specialize this construction to the Vlasov--Poisson system and obtain the self-consistent numerical flow through velocity-space quadrature, a discrete Poisson solve, field interpolation, and numerical integration of the frozen characteristic equations. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we prove that the self-consistent exact frozen flow for this system is a volume-preserving diffeomorphism. Temporal self-convergence tests on Vlasov--Poisson and guiding-center benchmarks yield rates consistent with the design orders and illustrate conservation behavior and the evolution of solution structures in long-time simulations with large time steps.
item.dc:creator: Xiaofeng Cai, Linghui Kong

item.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2610.35849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interaction of strong ($a_0>1$), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by $\varepsilon_{\rm B}\equiv a_0\omega_{\rm B}/\omega_0$, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For $\varepsilon_{\rm B}<1$ the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency $\Omega_{\rm B}$ to scattering; when $\Omega_{\rm B}$ exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm p}^{-2/3}$ to $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm B}^{1/2}/\varepsilon_{\rm p}$ wavelengths ($\varepsilon_{\rm p}\equiv a_0\omega_{\rm p}/\omega_0$; $\omega_{\rm p}$ is the plasma frequency). When $a_0^2>\varepsilon_{\rm B}>1$, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.
item.dc:creator: Navin Sridhar (Stanford University)

item.title: Omnigenous stellarators with improved ideal and kinetic ballooning stability
item.description: arXiv:2410.04576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Omnigenity is a property of a magnetic field which ensures confinement of trapped particles. It is a necessary requirement for any high-performance stellarator. After creating an omnigenous equilibrium, one must also ensure reduced transport resulting from kinetic and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities. To this end, we leverage the GPU-accelerated DESC optimization suite, which is used to design stable, finite-$\beta$ omnigenous equilibria with poloidal, toroidal, and helical symmetry, achieving Mercier, ideal ballooning, and as a consequence, improved kinetic ballooning stability. We discover stellarators with second stability, a regime of large pressure gradient where an equilibrium becomes ideal ballooning stable, and demonstrate and explore both using theory and gyrokinetic simulations the connection between ideal and kinetic ballooning stability.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Gaur, Rory Conlin, David Dickinson, Jason F. Parisi, Dario Panici, Daniel Dudt, Patrick Kim, Kaya Unalmis, William D. Dorland, Egemen Kolemen

item.title: Control of the bootstrap current in approximately quasi-axisymmetric magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2603.20125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quasi-axisymmetric stellarators are the stellarator analogue of axisymmetric tokamaks, retaining many of their favorable confinement properties, their compactness and their relative coil simplicity, while avoiding their principal limitation, the need for an inductively driven plasma current. Despite these attractive physics properties, the development of quasi-axisymmetric configurations has been severely constrained by the absence of an experimentally validated divertor concept compatible with their large bootstrap current. In this Letter, approximately quasi-axisymmetric fields, complemented with piecewise omnigenous perturbations, are proposed as the basis for a new strategy towards a stellarator reactor that potentially achieves, simultaneously, simple coil geometries, tokamak-like confinement and, through tailoring of the bootstrap current, compatibility with an island divertor. Implications for attaining a high bootstrap current fraction in tokamak devices are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: J. L. Velasco, I. Calvo, J. M. Garc\'ia-Rega\~na

item.title: Theory for the power threshold of the L-H transition in tokamaks
item.description: arXiv:2605.00624v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Flux-driven two-fluid simulations in a diverted tokamak exhibit a confinement transition when a critical heating threshold is exceeded, as in experimental observations of the L-H transition. The simulations show that electromagnetic drift-wave turbulence spontaneously generates a sheared $E\times B$ flow responsible for transport suppression in the edge. The toroidal-field asymmetry of the transition, here reproduced in simulations for the first time, arises from time-reversal symmetry breaking by finite collisionality, as demonstrated by a quasilinear calculation of the turbulent momentum flux. Scaling laws are analytically derived for the L-H power threshold in the high- and low-density branches, for the density minimum, and for the minimum power, all matching or surpassing the accuracy of existing empirical scalings.
item.dc:creator: Brenno De Lucca, Paolo Ricci, Benoit Labit, Davide Mancini, Louis Stenger, Zeno Tecchiolli

item.title: Feasibility of a Flexible, Hybrid Tokamak-Stellarator Experiment using an Axisymmetric Dipole Coil Array
item.description: arXiv:2606.13326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate the design of a flexible, university-scale hybrid tokamak-stellarator experiment based on an axisymmetric array of planar HTS dipole coils. Because the coil array has few geometric degrees of freedom, we use single-stage optimization of the coil currents initialized from two-stage solutions to obtain mutually consistent equilibria and coil sets within realistic engineering limits. We find that the field error and coil current thresholds set minimum and maximum coil-plasma distances that confine the boundary to a roughly fixed axisymmetric envelope, within which rotational transform, volume, coil current, and quasi-symmetry (QS) error trade off against one another. Tighter current limits delocalize the non-axisymmetric shaping and raise QS error at fixed transform. From this single coil array we obtain a broad range of equilibria-quasi-axisymmetric vacuum stellarators with $\iota$ up to 0.2, finite-$\beta$ hybrids with realistic profiles reaching on-axis $\iota$ $\approx$ 1 and vacuum transform relevant for MHD stabilization, and strongly shaped tokamaks with elongation $\kappa$ = 1.7 and triangularity $\delta$ = $\pm$0.6, all at peak pointwise coil forces well below the HTS tolerance. We show the same array can additionally correct toroidal field (TF) coil ripple, reducing the number of TF coils required compared to the equivalent tokamak. These results establish the design as a promising platform for hybrid tokamak-stellarator research.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Halpern, Mohammed Haque, Elizabeth Paul, Carlos Paz-Soldan, Rithik Banerjee, Talia Angles, Frederick Sheehan, Ian Stewart, Alan Kaptanoglu

item.title: Current-Sheet Formation in Electron Magnetohydrodynamics with Split Fractional Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2607.18648v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thin current sheets are central small-scale structures in electron magnetohydrodynamics (EMHD), closely associated with energy dissipation and fast magnetic reconnection at electron scales. We study their formation numerically in a $2\frac{1}{2}$-dimensional EMHD system on a periodic domain with split fractional dissipation, where the magnetic potential and the vertical magnetic component are damped separately. The local theory is governed by a symmetric combined damping balance, but the numerical onset of small-scale growth need not follow this symmetry. A scaling analysis identifies the out-of-plane current as the primary concentration observable, since it is regularized only through the magnetic-potential equation. Using a validated Fourier pseudospectral exponential time-differencing solver with resolution-controlled diagnostics, we find a clear decay/concentration dichotomy. The onset boundary is markedly asymmetric: current-sheet formation appears to be controlled mainly by damping of the magnetic potential, rather than by the combined damping strength. The analyticity strip collapses to the grid scale, the concentration sharpens under grid refinement, and the observed growth is consistent with an energy-critical self-similar rate, with exponent near three. These experiments indicate that magnetic-potential damping is the apparent binding constraint for current-sheet concentration, refining the symmetric sum picture.
item.dc:creator: Ruimeng Hu, Qirui Peng, Xu Yang

item.title: Trapping: The "Waterfall" of Vlasov-Poisson Dynamics and the Post-Transient Emergence of Drift-Independent Hole Structures in Collisionless Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2608.18658v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A key aspect of structure formation in collisionless plasmas is particle trapping or, more precisely, the gap this process leaves in the theoretical description. While the dynamics prior to the onset of trapping are governed by Landau physics and phase mixing, the full effects of nonlinearity only emerge during the trapping phase, for which an explicit description is lacking. Consequently, this gap divides the temporal evolution into a linear Vlasov-Poisson phase preceding the transition and a post-transient Vlasov-Poisson phase characterized by a wide spectrum of particle trapping scenarios and associated Schamel equilibria. Metaphorically, this trapping process can thus be compared to a waterfall in fluid dynamics, where, similarly, no explicit dynamic link can be established between the regions above and below the cascade. A second insight is that the Vlasov-Poisson mean-field description fails due to the separatrix singularity, which necessitates a temporary recourse to the BBGKY hierarchy. To resolve this problem of the singularity, an analysis using the method of matched asymptotic expansions is proposed. Applied to the singular boundary of the separatrix zone, this approach employs local smoothing techniques, such as those mediated by the two-particle correlation function. It offers a suitable mechanism for selecting hole equilibria in the post-transition phase. Furthermore, we report the existence of a spatially periodic Langmuir hole that vanishes if regularity requirements are too stringent, and we demonstrate that self-acceleration, accompanying the transition from a slow electron acoustic hole to a fast Langmuir hole, is driven by the release of particularly deeply trapped electrons.
item.dc:creator: Hans Schamel

item.title: Plasmon-polaritons in a rarefied nonrelativistic neutron gas
item.description: arXiv:2608.22177v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The electromagnetic properties of a dilute unpolarized nonrelativistic neutron gas are described in the case when neutron-by-neutron scattering is negligible. The Gaussian (Maxwell-Boltzmann) and Fermi-Dirac one-particle density matrices for the neutron gas are considered, the typical space scale of variations of these density matrices being assumed to be much larger than the typical space scale of variations of the electromagnetic field. The Green functions for the static effective Maxwell equations are obtained. It is shown that a rarefied neutron gas does not possess a ferromagnetic instability even in a nonequilibrium state. The analog of Friedel oscillations is described. The properties of plasmon-polaritons in the neutron gas are revealed. It turns out that the dispersion law of longitudinal and transverse plasmon-polaritons has an infinite number of branches at a given momentum. The region of parameters where the plasmon-polaritons can be regarded as quasiparticles is found. The plasmon-polaritons on a Gaussian wave packet of a single electron are described. Their dispersion law proves to have an infinite number of branches at a given momentum. It is shown that there exist stable longitudinal plasmon-polaritons even on a single electron.
item.dc:creator: P. O. Kazinski, A. M. Trushchuk

item.title: Bayesian inference of non-Maxwellian distribution functions from collective Thomson scattering spectra
item.description: arXiv:2609.31020v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate Bayesian inference of non-Maxwellian electron distribution functions from collective Thomson scattering (CTS) spectra. We represent distribution functions using multiple candidate models of different complexity and perform inference on synthetic spectra generated from known non-Maxwellian distribution functions. Our analysis demonstrates that a sufficiently flexible model can approximate the overall shape of the ground-truth distribution function. The most plausible model is identified based on model evidence, a statistical measure representing the probability to obtain the observed data given the model. When the candidates include the ground-truth model, the model evidence favors the ground-truth model. Without the ground-truth model as a candidate, the model evidence favors the candidate model with the fewest parameters that adequately approximates the data. The posterior probability density function of the most plausible model reveals the characteristic features and associated uncertainties of the underlying distribution function. The origin of the additional spectral peaks is attributed to a combination of modifications to the dispersion relation and reduced Landau damping. This enables the objective and data-driven identification of distribution functions directly from observed CTS spectra.
item.dc:creator: Kentaro Sakai, ByungJun Kang, Akito Nakano, Takeo Hoshi

item.title: Stellarators Linking Axisymmetric Mirrors Part 1: Coil Design, MHD Equilibrium, and Physics Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.06085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a computational design study of a stellarator-mirror hybrid concept, Stellarators Linking Axisymmetric Mirrors (SLAMs), in which an optimized poloidally omnigenous (OP or QI) stellarator serves as the rotational-transform-generating element that links long, axisymmetric (circular cross-section) magnetic mirrors. Starting from an OP precursor configuration obtained from the DESC omnigenity database, we construct hybrid coil sets for field period nFP = 2 SLAMs by separating the OP modular coils along the device midplane and inserting axisymmetric planar mirror coils into the resulting gap. Field-line tracing shows that nested vacuum flux surfaces survive this extrusion across a range of mirror-section lengths, with the cross-section qualitatively preserved at the point where the mirror is inserted. We use the field-line tracing data to map the shape of a surface and use the GVEC fixed-boundary solver to calculate an ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equilibrium and evaluate physics metrics such as the neoclassical transport proxy ($\epsilon_{\rm eff}^{3/2}$), the vacuum magnetic well (W), and the gyrokinetic heat fluxes (Q), providing a first-principles analysis of such concepts using modern stellarator analysis tools.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Gaur, Djin Patch, Robert Babin, Florian Hindenlang, Xu Chu, Tony Qian

item.title: Role of interchange and mixed modes in magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor instability dynamics --- a 2D vs 3D study
item.description: arXiv:2510.27053v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor instability (MRTI) governs plasma mixing and transport in diverse systems. Owing to computational constraints, two-dimensional (2D) MRTI simulations are common. It is intuitive that 2D and three-dimensional (3D) counterparts differ significantly. One of the crucial differences is the types of wave modes admissible in the two systems. Perturbations in 3D MRTI facilitate the coexistence of interchange, undular, and mixed modes. Such rich physics is not possible in 2D, where the perturbations can only have undular modes. This raises the question, how do the interchange and mixed modes change the MRTI dynamics? To address this aspect, we simulate MRTI in 2D and 3D, across different magnetic field strengths. Consequently, this paper provides, currently lacking, a rigorous qualitative and quantitative evaluation of the similarities and differences between 2D and 3D MRTI. The 2D MRTI is characterized by large-scale plumes with inefficient mixing and significant fluid interpenetration, while the 3D is characterized by significant mixing and small-scale plumes. Consequently, higher gravitational potential energy is extracted in 2D. The small-scale vortices and large current sheets lead to higher energy dissipation in 3D. Extending to fundamental nature of evolution, 3D simulations tend towards a self-similar state (due to interchange and mixed modes). But such behaviour was not observed in our 2D simulations, due to the persistent influence of magnetic field. Surprisingly, the reconnection driven magnetic-to-kinetic energy conversion is similar in 2D and 3D. Overall, the work concludes that interchange and mixed modes influence the dynamics significantly leading to stark differences between 2D and 3D MRTI. The work thus guides the extent to which one can extrapolate the 2D simulations results to understand MRTI in astrophysical and fusion energy systems.
item.dc:creator: Manohar Teja Kalluri, Andrew Hillier

item.title: Equation of State for warm Neutron Star outer crusts
item.description: arXiv:2604.18136v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the equation of state (EoS) of a warm ion plasma as obtained by performing microscopic many-body simulations using Molecular Dynamics computational techniques. Using the cold one-component plasma (OCP) composition in the Neutron Star (NS) outer crust assumed in \cite{Murarka_2022} with a representative heavy nucleus for each density, we refine previous calculations. We include electron screening and modeling of ions as finite-size Gaussian distributions in the interaction potential, together with an efficient Ewald energy summation procedure. From this, the EoS relation $P(n_B,T)$ is obtained as a function of baryonic number density $n_B\in[7.48\times 10^{-10},2.09\times10^{-4}]$ $ \rm fm^{-3}$ and temperature $k_{B}T\in[1,5]$ MeV in the NS outer crust conditions. In order to improve the usability of our results we provide tabulated data values along with a neural network parametrization available in the Zenodo repository, see https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15348712. We find that even at moderate temperatures, thermal effects of ions are key in the higher density region closer to the inner crust, when described using a thermal effective parametrization based on the thermal adiabatic index $\Gamma_{th}$. We compare our results with other EoS in the literature performing a critical discussion.
item.dc:creator: David Barba-Gonz\'alez, Conrado Albertus, M. \'Angeles P\'erez-Garc\'ia
